results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains multiple types of Kenyon cells. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, there are [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cells, including specific types such as [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as gamma Kenyon cells. Furthermore, Virtual Fly Brain summarizes that the main subtypes of Kenyon cells include alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes like core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and others, as referenced by Lee et al., 1999, and Aso et al., 2014. VFB holds extensive data on Kenyon cells, including [31468](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") images, scRNAseq data, transgene expression data, and both downstream and upstream connectivity classes.

results.title: Gene expression
results.question: What neurotransmitter do mushroom body Kenyon cells use?
results.response: Mushroom body Kenyon cells use acetylcholine as their primary neurotransmitter, according to the VFB database, which supports this based on its neurotransmitter tags indicating that Kenyon cells are cholinergic.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response:
The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which states that any antennal lobe projection neuron that sends synaptic output to the mushroom body, and describes axons to higher brain centers, generally the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the antennal lobe, including images, neuron data, and information on parts and subclasses of the antennal lobe, as well as data on tracts and nerves innervating it, and lineage clones found in it.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
The question pertains to the Drosophila central complex, but the provided Resolved Entities and AVAILABLE VFB DATA are related to the [common oviduct](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004913 "Open common oviduct in Virtual Fly Brain"), which is not relevant to the central complex. 

However, I can provide general information about the Drosophila central complex. The Drosophila central complex is a structure in the insect brain that has been implicated in various functions, including spatial memory, visual navigation, and locomotor control (as discussed in literature, such as in Heinze and Homberg, 2007; Wolff et al., 2015; and Seelig and Jayaraman, 2015). The main components of the central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the noduli, and the protocerebral bridge.

Since the AVAILABLE VFB DATA does not contain information about the central complex, but rather about the common oviduct, with [4](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004913,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of common oviduct") records of parts of the common oviduct, it appears that VFB has more information about the common oviduct than the central complex. 

It is worth noting that the information provided here about the central complex comes from general knowledge and literature, rather than from the VFB database or the provided EVIDENCE.

results.title: Circuit motif

results.response: Dopaminergic input to mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) comes from various types of dopaminergic neurons, including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons and adult dopaminergic PAM neurons, as well as dopaminergic PPL1 neurons (VFB). Specifically, VFB found 77 upstream class-connectivity partners matching "dopaminergic neuron" for MBON, including adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron, adult dopaminergic PAM neuron, dopaminergic PPL1 neuron, dopaminergic PAM neuron 6, and dopaminergic PAM neuron 8. The exact connections between specific types of DANs and MBONs are not fully detailed in the available information, but VFB does hold extensive data on the connectivity of MBONs, including [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes and [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes. Additionally, there are [69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") subclasses of MBON, suggesting a complex and potentially specific relationship between different types of DANs and MBONs (VFB).

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response: The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron with a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer. It detects looming (expansion) stimuli and projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. Its activity elicits a jump escape response. LPLC2 is also known to have connections to various neurons, including adult cholinergic neurons, T5c neurons, and transmedullary neurons. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which provides a summary of the neuron's profile, including its morphology, function, and connections, as described in publications by Wu et al., 2016, and Klapoetke et al., 2017.

The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult Drosophila is more elaborated than in larval Drosophila. According to VFB, the [adult antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007401 "Open adult antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas the larval antennal lobe has around 22 glomeruli. This information comes from the VFB database, as stated in VFB reference. 

VFB holds a range of data related to the antennal lobe, including images, neuron information, parts of the antennal lobe, and lineage clones found in the antennal lobe. For example, there are [6](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of antennal lobe") available images of antennal lobe, and [676](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003924,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe") neurons with some part in antennal lobe.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?

The literature suggests that there are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs), as reported by (Aso et al., 2014) and (Cervantes-Sandoval et al., 2017), but the specific claim of reciprocal connections comes from the VFB database. According to the VFB database, VFB found 22 reciprocal class-level pairs between [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") and [dopaminergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005131 "Open dopaminergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). The direction from dopaminergic neuron to mushroom body output neuron has a partner count of 77, while the direction from mushroom body output neuron to dopaminergic neuron has a partner count of 94. The source-to-target weight is 10963 and the target-to-source weight is 7620.

VFB holds extensive data on both mushroom body output neuron and dopaminergic neuron, including images, subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and downstream and upstream connectivity classes. For mushroom body output neuron, VFB has [993](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of MBON") available images, [69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") subclasses, [1](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for MBON") scRNAseq data, [157](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in MBON") transgene expressions, [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes, and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes. For dopaminergic neuron, VFB has [61070](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of dopaminergic neuron") available images, [189](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of dopaminergic neuron") subclasses, [58](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for dopaminergic neuron") scRNAseq data, [227](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in dopaminergic neuron") transgene expressions, [8845](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") downstream connectivity classes, and [7914](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") upstream connectivity classes.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
The pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") involves intermediate neuron types, specifically antennal lobe projection neurons, which connect olfactory receptor neurons to the adult lateral horn. According to the VFB database, a high-level pathway is [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> adult lateral horn. 

VFB holds a range of data relevant to this pathway, including downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron ([575](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") records) and upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron ([379](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") records), which could provide further details on the connections between these neuron types. Additionally, VFB has extensive data on neurons with some part in adult lateral horn ([1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") records), including those with synaptic terminals ([1658](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") records), presynaptic terminals ([816](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") records), and postsynaptic terminals ([1375](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") records) in this region, which may help elucidate the specific connections within the pathway. 

The literature supports the role of antennal lobe projection neurons as intermediates in this pathway (as stated in VFB).

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The anatomical containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database, which provides a detailed hierarchical structure of the Drosophila brain. 

According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 is contained within the adult antennal lobe, which is part of the adult deutocerebrum. The adult deutocerebrum is then contained within the adult cerebrum, which is part of the adult central brain. Finally, the adult central brain is contained within the adult brain, which is the top-level brain structure. 

The Virtual Fly Brain database also contains additional information about the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including neurons with some part in this glomerulus ([10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records), neurons with synaptic terminals in this glomerulus (10 records), and images of neurons with some part in this glomerulus ([911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") records). However, the specific hierarchical structure is based on the containment chain provided by the Virtual Fly Brain database.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). According to the VFB database, it has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. The giant fiber neuron has a large descending axon and arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. It also has dendritic arborization in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The neuron enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally and ends abruptly without branching. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge.

As for its connectivity, the giant fiber neuron receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons, as reported by Kim et al. (2020). VFB holds downstream connectivity classes for the giant fiber neuron ([361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) and upstream connectivity classes ([435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records), which can be used to further explore its connections.

There are available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron, with [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. Additionally, VFB has [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, which can be used to visualize its anatomy.

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Kim et al. (2020), among others. These studies provide further information on the anatomy, connectivity, and function of the giant fiber neuron.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: Based on connectivity data from VFB, neuron types such as [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), [T4ai neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052241 "Open T4ai neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB data suggest that adult visual projection neurons could be involved in this connection, as they have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body. The presence of neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals in both the visual system and the mushroom body, as well as tracts and nerves innervating the mushroom body, further supports the possibility of a connection between these two systems. VFB holds extensive data on neurons with parts in the visual system ([1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system")) and the mushroom body ([602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body")), including synaptic terminals and expression patterns, which could be used to further investigate this potential connection. Overall, the available data suggest that visual information could indeed reach the memory circuit via neurons that connect the visual system and the mushroom body.
